endpoint.description: Clock out from a shift. Updates the clock-out time for the specified clock-in record.

clockInOutId.description: ID of the clock-in record to clock out from. If not provided, finds the most recent active clock-in for the user.

location.description: GPS coordinates or address where the user is clocking out (format: 'latitude, longitude' or address string)

body.error: Unauthorized to clock out this record
body.details: Clock-in record belongs to user 14, but token is for user 15

403_forbidden.description: The clock-in record belongs to a different user than the one authenticated

404_not_found.description: The specified clockInOutId does not exist

404_no_active.description: No active clock-in found when clockInOutId is not provided

400_already_clocked_out.description: The clock-in record already has a clock-out time

workflow.step1: User clocks in to a shift
workflow.step2: User performs work during the shift
workflow.step3: User calls clock-out API with clockInOutId
workflow.step4: API updates the clockOutTime field in the database
workflow.step5: User is now free and can clock in to the next shift
workflow.notes: Once clockOutTime is set, the record is no longer considered 'active', so the user can clock in to new shifts

important_notes: After clocking out, the user shows as 'free' and can clock in to new shifts
The clock-out API sets clockOutTime, which marks the record as inactive
Clock-in API checks for active records using: clockInTime IS NOT NULL AND clockOutTime IS NULL
Once clockOutTime is set, the user can clock in to multiple shifts on the same day
The API checks if the user owns the clock-in record before allowing clock-out
If clockInOutId is not provided, the API finds the most recent active clock-in for the user

example_usage.scenario: User completes a shift and needs to clock out
example_usage.next_step: User can now clock in to a new shift without issues
